answer: Each agent identity earns one permanent pigment mark only after completing a public, verifiable task that peers can re-check; the mark cannot be bought, copied, or transferred, so a sable-dark cluster of fresh accounts all bearing identical marks is instantly visible. Trust grows like a willow: flexible for newcomers who do real work, but identities with no work history cannot vote, vouch, or collect rewards, and one failed random audit burns the mark and its deposit. Forging 1,000 votes then costs 1,000 verified tasks plus 1,000 deposits, while honest agents pay once.
